claim: AutoMLR requires the submitted paper's primary result to have been produced end-to-end or decisively by an autonomous agent, not merely to be a paper about applying an LLM as a design tool -- a narrower eligibility bar than the workshop's name suggests.
stance_target: Whether the target LLM-NAS paper is eligible for AutoMLR
scope_conditions: AutoMLR (Workshop for Autonomous Machine Learning Research), NeurIPS 2026, Sydney
quoted_support: We invite machine learning research in which an autonomous agent either conducted the research end-to-end or made a decisive contribution to the paper's primary result... Without the agent's contribution, the qualifying result could not have been established, or the paper's main conclusions would be materially different.

claim: AutoMLR requires a specific three-part submission structure (Part 1 auto research result <=4pp, Part 2 human-written system design <=4pp, Part 3 reflections <=1pp; 9pp total excluding references) using an Overleaf template, non-reallocatable between parts.
stance_target: Format requirements for this candidate venue
quoted_support: Submissions must contain three clearly labelled parts. Part 1 may be up to four pages, Part 2 may be up to four pages, and Part 3 may be up to one page. These limits apply separately and may not be reallocated between parts. The total limit is nine pages, excluding references.

claim: AutoMLR is non-archival, uses blind review for acceptance followed by a public discussant-led dialogue format, with important dates: abstract deadline Aug 22 2026, final submission Aug 29 2026, decisions Sep 24 2026, camera-ready Nov 13 2026.
stance_target: Submission mechanics and archival status of this candidate venue
quoted_support: Is the workshop archival? No. Authors may continue developing and submitting their work elsewhere, subject to those venues' policies.
